chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The food of one is sufficient for two, and the food of two is sufficient for three, and the food of three is sufficient for four.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic teaching on sharing food and the sufficiency of meals for multiple people?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) conveys the Prophet’s (PBUH) teaching on the spiritual and physical blessings of sharing food, emphasizing that divine barakah multiplies sustenance when distributed communally. It serves as a foundational principle for Islamic social etiquette, encouraging generosity and mitigating scarcity through collective consumption. This concept is often cited by Shia scholars to illustrate the transformative power of intention and sharing in daily life.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Gayas Bin Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saw</sup> said a meal for one should suffice the two, and a meal for the two should suffice the three, and a meal for the three should suffice the four’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause,
has said, ‘Food for one is sufficient for two, food for two is sufficient for three and food for three is sufficient for four people.”’
